business_ops.seasonality: Seasonality in jewellery buying is a key demand driver: weddings, festivals and harvests (in rural regions) are the main drivers, tying demand to particular months and seasons. The Company drives festive sales during key occasions such as Gudi Padwa, Akshay Tritiya, Dussehra and Diwali, as well as new-age occasions like Valentine's Day; key cities contribute high sales particularly during Diwali. Jewellery collections are launched time-bound for specified festive periods with maximum revenue contribution and are merged into regular stock once the period passes.

supplier_concentration.note: Top-3 third-party suppliers as a percentage of total purchases of stock-in-trade (not of revenue): purchases of ₹427.61 mn (FY23), ₹511.47 mn (FY24), ₹594.19 mn (FY25) and ₹657.47 mn (H1 FY26). The DRHP references a top-10 suppliers disclosure, but no top-1/top-5/top-10 percentages appear in the routed text.

business_ops.supply_chain_integration: No backward integration: the Company does not manufacture any products in-house (no revenue from manufacturing activities in FY23–FY25 and H1 FY26). It acquires finished diamond and gemstone-studded jewellery directly from various third-party manufacturing partners and Karigars in India — sourcing is limited to finished products from domestic manufacturing partners; no direct import/export of raw materials such as diamonds, gemstones or precious metals, except customer-provided gold for specific design orders. Purchases of stock-in-trade from manufacturing partners: ₹1,392.64 mn (70.04% of revenue from operations) in FY23, ₹1,663.63 mn (85.04%) in FY24, ₹1,971.41 mn (76.36%) in FY25 and ₹2,485.72 mn (158.61%) in H1 FY26. Design is partly in-house (dual design approach: in-house design studio staffed with 2 designers as of September 30, 2025, plus curated selections and joint design initiatives with third-party manufacturers). Forward/retail infrastructure is leveraged from Corporate Promoter P. N. Gadgil & Sons Limited under a Franchise Agreement dated February 1, 2025 (amended June 26, 2025) — retail space, logistics, electricity, furniture, security and billing software; under the FOFO model inventory is transferred to the Corporate Promoter, which retails the products under the Reva brand. The diamond business itself was acquired from the Corporate Promoter via a slump-sale Business Transfer Agreement dated January 31, 2025 (inventory ₹1,627.67 mn and gratuity liability ₹4.67 mn transferred; net value ₹1,623.01 mn; lump-sum consideration ₹1,62,30,09,000). Quality control practices across the value chain include specialised tools for assessing clarity, cut, colour, carat weight and metal purity, and regular supply-chain audits. Concentrated regional footprint enables centralised inventory management, distribution and optimised transport routes through its logistics service provider.

Regional demand insights allow tailored collections and festive-season sales during occasions such as Gudi Padwa, Akshay Tritiya, Dussehra, Diwali and new-age occasions like Valentine's Day
strengths: Brand value of 'Reva' and Promoter legacy: Corporate Promoter P. N. Gadgil & Sons Limited brings more than 190 years of experience (CARE Report), Individual Promoters Govind Gadgil and Renu Gadgil bring 45 and 13 years respectively in the jewellery industry
Majority of Stores operate within retail infrastructure owned by the Corporate Promoter with an established sales and logistics network, reducing capital investment needs in the initial phase
Experienced Board and management: Whole-Time Director and CEO Amit Yeshwant Modak has 25 years of experience in the jewellery industry; 69 permanent employees

Regional expertise across Tier-1, Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities in Maharashtra, Gujarat and Karnataka: concentrated footprint enables lower logistics costs, favourable inventory turnover, centralised inventory management and faster replenishment cycles
Diversified product portfolio across categories and price points catering to a wide spectrum of consumer preferences

Materially higher profitability than DRHP-listed peers: Fiscal 2025 Adjusted EBITDA margin 30.83% and PAT margin 23.04% versus peers' 4.46%-6.60% and 2.42%-2.61% respectively (DRHP KPI comparison table)
threats: Intense competition in the Indian jewellery market from domestic and multinational players; DRHP names Bluestone Jewellery and Lifestyle Private Limited, Caratlane Trading Private Limited, Orra Fine Jewellery Private Limited, Senco Gold Limited and Thangamayil Jewellery Limited as competitors (CARE Report)

Many competitors possess longer operational histories, larger customer and supplier networks, stronger brand recognition and greater financial and operational resources, enabling heavier investment in inventory, store expansion, marketing and distribution

Regulatory changes: restrictions and duties on import of bullion and precious stones, GST rate or compliance changes, hallmarking norms and mandatory PAN disclosure for high-value transactions could raise costs or dampen demand
ESG and responsible-sourcing scrutiny (including Kimberley Process compliance) with reliance on suppliers and third parties for adherence to sourcing standards
Risk of imitation of unregistered jewellery designs diluting brand identity and competitive edge
weaknesses: Dependence on Corporate Promoter P. N. Gadgil & Sons Limited: majority of Stores operate within its physical retail infrastructure and the Company leverages its sales and logistics network and customer base
Very low advertising spend historically (0.55% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2025; 0.07% in H1 FY26) while brand positioning depends on effective marketing
Jewellery designs are not registered under the Designs Act, 2000, limiting recourse against imitation
Short operating history in corporate form: formed by conversion of an erstwhile partnership firm on December 20, 2024; no EPS or NAV presented for Fiscal 2024 and Fiscal 2023
Some Directors have no experience of being directors in any other listed entity in India
No dividends paid to Shareholders to date
Revenue declined 1.62% year-on-year in Fiscal 2024 before growing 31.97% in Fiscal 2025 (DRHP KPI table)

overview.business_model: Sells retail diamond jewellery (diamond-studded jewellery, gold, silver, platinum and related articles per its main object) through physical stores under the flagship 'Reva' brand, including a brand-exclusive company-owned company-operated (COCO) store debuted in Wakad, Pune. The business was acquired from corporate promoter P. N. Gadgil & Sons Limited on a going-concern slump-sale basis for a consideration of Rs 1,623.01 million (BTA dated January 31, 2025; full amount of Rs 1,670.96 million including applicable taxes paid before March 31, 2025, entirely in cash via NEFT/RTGS), and the company operates pursuant to a Franchise Agreement dated February 1, 2025 (amended June 26, 2025) with P. N. Gadgil & Sons Limited. Revenue is heavily concentrated in Maharashtra: Rs 2,503.83 million (96.97% of revenue from operations) in Fiscal 2025 and Rs 1,528.70 million (97.54%) in the six months ended September 30, 2025.

concerns_observed: Deep promoter entanglement: the entire diamond business was acquired from Corporate Promoter P. N. Gadgil & Sons Limited via a slump-sale Business Transfer Agreement dated January 31, 2025 for Rs 1,623.01 million (Rs 1,670.96 million including taxes, settled in cash before March 31, 2025), and the company operates under a Franchise Agreement dated February 1, 2025 (amended June 26, 2025) with the same promoter for retail space, logistics, electricity, furniture, security and billing software.

Reconstructed track record: financials for FY23-FY25 are the transferred diamond business combined as if from April 1, 2022 under Ind AS 103 Appendix C (common control); the DRHP itself states the track record is 'technically reconstructed and should not be interpreted as the independent operating history of our Company' (company incorporated December 20, 2024).

Negative pre-conversion net worth: total equity of Rs (520.17) million (FY23) and Rs (284.96) million (FY24); a negative capital reserve of Rs (1,461.46) million was recognised on the common-control BTA.

Geographic concentration: Maharashtra contributed 96.73%/96.75%/96.97%/97.54% of revenue across FY23/FY24/FY25/H1FY26; top-5 stores contributed 43.93% of FY25 revenue and the single largest store (Chinchwad PCMC) 11.77%.

Entire pre-issue capital of 21,866,400 shares was built within about five months of incorporation, including a 350:100 bonus issue (17,007,200 shares) on May 21, 2025 that falls inside the 18-month regulatory window before the RHP.
Low weighted-average cost of acquisition of equity shares (auditor-certified): Rs 49.40 (last one year) and Rs 42.81 (last 18 months / three years), acquisition price range Nil-Rs 750.

High and rising working-capital intensity: cash conversion cycle of 435.4 days and inventory of 498.5 days in H1FY26; operating cash flow turned negative at Rs (546.71) million in H1FY26 versus PAT of Rs 201.33 million, driven by inventory build-up.

Debt built from zero: total borrowings Rs 1,302.49 million as at September 30, 2025 (nil in FY23/FY24), partly a supply-creditor liability to the Corporate Promoter under the BTA plus Rs 900.00 million from Federal Bank; secured by charge over movable/immovable property and Individual Promoter personal guarantees.

Related-party transactions in H1FY26 exceeded 10% of preceding-year turnover: sale of goods to P. N. Gadgil & Sons Rs 134.40 million and commission expense Rs 62.13 million; an unsecured Rs 250.00 million promoter loan was taken and repaid within the period.

Objects execution unstarted: 100% of the store fit-out and equipment capex is on pending quotations with no purchase orders placed, no lease/licence agreements signed and no site locations identified; fund requirements were not appraised by any bank or financial institution.

Margin compression in the latest stub: EBITDA margin fell from 30.8% (FY25) to 19.6% (H1FY26) and PAT margin from 23.0% to 12.8%, with lower-margin gold sales (nil before) reaching 14.12% of H1FY26 revenue.

Structural dependence and thin capabilities: no in-house manufacturing, no e-commerce revenue, a 2-person in-house design team, advertising spend of just 0.55% of revenue (FY25) and 0.07% (H1FY26), and unregistered jewellery designs; sole BRLM (Smart Horizon Capital Advisors).

open_questions: What are the renewal, termination and exclusivity terms of the Franchise Agreement with P. N. Gadgil & Sons, and what is the continuity risk to the 33 shop-in-shop stores if it lapses or is renegotiated?
How was the Rs 1,623.01 million slump-sale consideration for the diamond business valued, and on what basis is a common-control transfer between related parties represented as arm's-length?
Why did EBITDA and PAT margins compress so sharply in H1FY26 (to 19.6% and 12.8%), and is the negative operating cash flow of Rs -546.71 million structural to the expansion phase?
What explains the company's ~30%+ EBITDA margin when DRHP-identified listed peers report 4.46%-6.60%, and is that gap sustainable at scale?
What will post-issue promoter holding be, and how does the eventual offer price compare with the WACA of Rs 42.81-49.40 and the May 2025 bonus?

Given 100% of store capex is unordered and no sites are identified, what is a realistic deployment schedule for the Rs 2,865.64 million across Fiscals 2026-2028, and what is the cost-overrun exposure?

What are the full terms of the recurring RPT sale-of-goods (Rs 134.40 mn) and commission (Rs 62.13 mn) arrangements with the Corporate Promoter, and are any back-to-back customer fund flows captured in the RPT disclosures?
What is the status and quantum of the Rs 273.90 million material civil litigation against the Promoters and its potential bearing on the company?

parameter_scores.basis: Whole business carved from Corporate Promoter P. N. Gadgil & Sons via slump-sale BTA (Rs 1,623.01 mn); operates under a Franchise Agreement with the same promoter; 33 of 34 stores are shop-in-shop within promoter premises; 'PNGS' word and Class 14/35 trademarks used without consideration under NOC; RPTs exceeded 10% of turnover in H1FY26.

Restated financials are a reconstructed common-control combination (Ind AS 103 Appendix C from April 1, 2022) that the DRHP says is not the company's independent operating history; company incorporated December 20, 2024; auditor Rule 11(g) qualification on payroll-software audit trail; no EPS/NAV disclosed for FY23/FY24.

Negative net worth in FY23 (Rs -520.17 mn) and FY24 (Rs -284.96 mn); negative capital reserve Rs -1,461.46 mn; CCC 435.4 days and inventory 498.5 days in H1FY26; operating cash flow Rs -546.71 mn in H1FY26; borrowings up to Rs 1,302.49 mn from nil.

FY2025 EBITDA margin 30.83% and PAT margin 23.04% far exceed DRHP peers (4.46%-6.60% / 2.42%-2.61%), but H1FY26 margins compressed to 19.6% / 12.8% and the peer gap itself invites scrutiny on sustainability.
Revenue Rs 1,988.48 mn (FY23) to Rs 2,581.83 mn (FY25), CAGR 13.95%, but FY24 declined 1.62% year-on-year; growth is lumpy and H1FY26 includes new gold-resale revenue (14.12%) not present earlier.
Maharashtra ~97% of revenue in every period (96.97% FY25, 97.54% H1FY26); top-5 stores 43.93% and largest single store 11.77% of FY25 revenue; only 1 store each in Gujarat and Karnataka.

Asset-light footprint depends on the Corporate Promoter's infrastructure and franchise agreement; no in-house manufacturing, no e-commerce, 2-person design team, unregistered designs, and rising lab-grown-diamond competition (India LGD jewellery market Rs 21,588 mn CY22 to Rs 28,558 mn CY24 per CARE).

Six-member board with 3 independent directors (one a former PNGS independent director) and standard committees; nil litigation against the company itself; offset by promoter dominance (83.04% pre-issue), overlapping directorships across promoter-group entities, some directors with no listed-company experience, and the auditor Rule 11(g) observation.

Rs 2,865.64 mn store capex has 100% of quotations pending with no purchase orders, no signed leases and no identified sites; deployment spread over Fiscals 2026-2028; not appraised by any bank or financial institution.
parameter_scores.parameter: Objects of issue and execution readiness

parameter_scores.basis: 100% fresh issue (up to Rs 3,800 mn) with no OFS avoids promoter cash-out and no shares pledged; but the 350:100 bonus (17,007,200 shares, May 21, 2025) sits inside the 18-month window, entire capital was created within ~5 months, and WACA is only Rs 42.81-49.40.

Issue price not yet determined and P/E not applicable pre-listing; DRHP-issuer row shows bonus-adjusted EPS Rs 35.21, NAV Rs 45.82 and RoNW 59.36% (inclusive of capital reserve/partner capital) against peer P/E range 15.74-80.96 (average 43.23) — comparability limited pending the price band.

Nil proceedings by or against the company; but material civil litigation of Rs 273.90 mn against Promoters and 2 tax proceedings (Rs 3.74 mn) against a director-promoter; aggregate litigation Rs 2,741.5 lakh equals 136.17% of PAT and 22.79% of net worth; trademark (Class 14/35) and design registrations still pending.

red_flags: The business is a January-2025 carve-out from the Corporate Promoter with common-control reconstructed financials that the DRHP itself states 'should not be interpreted as the independent operating history of our Company'.
Negative standalone net worth pre-FY25 (Rs -520.17 mn in FY23, Rs -284.96 mn in FY24) and a negative capital reserve of Rs -1,461.46 mn arising from the slump-sale accounting.

100% of the Rs 2,865.64 million store-expansion capex is unordered - no purchase orders, no signed leases, no identified sites and no bank/FI appraisal - so the entire use of proceeds carries execution risk.
A 350:100 bonus issue (17,007,200 shares) on May 21, 2025 inside the 18-month window inflated pre-issue capital, while the weighted-average cost of acquisition is only Rs 42.81-49.40.

Structural single-counterparty dependence: 33 of 34 stores sit inside Corporate Promoter premises and the Franchise Agreement controls inventory, logistics, infrastructure and even the planned online channel.
Sharp H1FY26 deterioration: operating cash flow of Rs -546.71 million, CCC of 435.4 days, borrowings up to Rs 1,302.49 million from nil, and margins roughly halved versus FY25.
strengths_observed: Reported profitability materially above DRHP-listed peers: Fiscal 2025 Adjusted EBITDA margin 30.83% and PAT margin 23.04% versus peers' 4.46%-6.60% and 2.42%-2.61% (DRHP KPI comparison table); FY2025 PAT of Rs 594.74 million on revenue of Rs 2,581.83 million.
Top-line growth over the reconstructed track record: revenue from operations rose from Rs 1,988.48 million (FY23) to Rs 2,581.83 million (FY25), a CAGR of 13.95%, after a 1.62% dip in FY24.

Issue is a 100% fresh issue of up to Rs 3,800 million with no offer-for-sale component, so no promoter/selling-shareholder cash-out; proceeds earmarked for 15 new brand-exclusive stores (Rs 2,865.64 million) and marketing (Rs 354.0 million).
No promoter shares pledged or encumbered as on the RHP date; all promoter shares fully paid-up and dematerialised.

Asset-light initial footprint: 33 of 34 stores operate as shop-in-shop within Corporate Promoter P. N. Gadgil & Sons' existing retail outlets, lowering upfront capex; products carry IGI (diamonds), GIA (solitaires) and BIS hallmark (gold) certifications.
Brand and operating lineage from Corporate Promoter P. N. Gadgil & Sons (190+ years per CARE Report); Individual Promoters cite 45 and 13 years in the jewellery trade and CEO Amit Modak 25 years.
